conditions.method: UPS, He I 21.22 eV, 45 degree take-off, -7 V sample bias
conditions.note: the paper does not state which MoS2 sample the UPS spectra used

source.detail: "Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) analysis shows a shift in the work function, correlating with the Schottky barrier height modification from 3.38 eV to 3.94 eV" (Fig. 3j caption, p. 5). X. Hou, W. Zhang, S. Duan, T. Jin, X. Geng, M. Lin, Y. Cai, J. Mao, Y. Luo, J. Zhu, J. Lin, W. Chen, Nat. Commun. 16, 9506 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41467-025-64579-5 [NOTE: 3.38 eV is the value before the oxygen-plasma treatment. The caption calls the change a barrier modification, but the two values are UPS work functions: a barrier cannot exceed the about 1.8 eV gap the paper measures by STS (Fig. 3e), and the main text gives their 0.56 eV difference as the barrier between oxidized and pristine MoS2 (p. 3). The difference also cancels any offset common to the two cutoffs. UPS used He I light (21.22 eV) at a 45 degree take-off angle with the sample at -7 V (Methods, p. 10). The paper does not say which MoS2 sample the UPS spectra used. Quoted text stays with its rights holders; the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.]
